program.name: Athletic Engine: 3-Day Performance
program.description: A 3-day athletic performance program designed to build explosive lower body power, rotational core stability, vertical jump, and work capacity.
guidelines: Perform all power exercises (jumps, push press, swings) first while neurologically fresh.
Move every rep with explosive intent.
Rest 2–3 minutes on power and compound lifts.

workouts.title: Lower Power
workouts.focus: Trap bar deadlift power, vertical box jumps, unilateral acceleration

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
cues: Stand centered between handles with feet hip-to-shoulder-width; grip center of handles.
Drop hips into a hybrid hinge-squat, chest proud, lats engaged to set spine neutral.
Drive the floor away through mid-foot with explosive intent.
Stand tall to full hip and knee lockout, squeezing glutes at the top.
avoid: Rounding lower back during the initial break off the floor.
Starting with hips too high (stiff-legging) or too low (shoving knees into handles).
Shrugging shoulders or hyperextending spine at lockout.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
cues: Place laces of rear foot on bench; step front foot forward into a balanced split stance.
Maintain a slight forward torso lean (~15°) with a braced, neutral spine.
Descend until back knee hovers an inch above the floor, front knee tracking over toes.
Drive straight up through the whole front foot (tripod foot: heel, big toe, pinky toe).
avoid: Front heel lifting off floor or front knee caving inward (valgus collapse).
Pushing aggressively off rear foot instead of loading the front working leg.
Hyperextending lower back by trying to stay unnaturally upright.

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
cues: Stand tall with a shoulder-width grip, lats engaged to keep bar pinned against thighs.
Soften knees slightly and lock that knee angle in place throughout the rep.
Push hips straight back horizontally as if reaching for a wall behind you.
Stop descent once hips stop moving backward (usually mid-shin), then drive hips forward.
avoid: Rounding lower back to reach the floor once hips have stopped traveling back.
Bending knees further into a squat, shifting tension away from hamstrings.
Allowing bar to drift forward away from legs.

exercises.name: Standing Machine Calf Raise
cues: Place balls of feet on edge of block, shoulder-width; keep knees straight with a micro-bend.
Lower heels as deep as ankle mobility allows; hold a full 2-second stretch at the bottom.
Drive up forcefully through the balls of feet, focusing pressure through the big toes.
Squeeze calves hard at peak contraction for 1 second before descending.
avoid: Bouncing out of bottom stretch (relies on Achilles tendon elasticity instead of muscle).
Bending and extending knees to heave weight up (turning it into a squat).
Rolling ankles outward onto pinky toes.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
cues: Stand perpendicular to cable in an athletic shoulder-width stance, knees slightly bent.
Hold handle with both hands tight against center of chest, core braced and ribs down.
Press handle straight forward until arms are fully extended, resisting all rotational pull.
Hold at full extension for 2 seconds, then return hands slowly to chest.
avoid: Allowing torso, shoulders, or hips to rotate toward the pulley.
Shrugging shoulders up toward ears during the press.
Rushing through reps without pausing at full extension.

workouts.title: Upper Power
workouts.focus: Push press power, weighted pull-up strength, and horizontal row capacity

exercises.name: Push Press
cues: Set bar in front rack across shoulders, hands just outside shoulders, core braced.
Dip knees 3–4 inches vertically, keeping torso strictly upright (do not hinge forward).
Explosively extend hips, knees, and ankles to drive the bar off shoulders.
Finish the press overhead with arms locked firmly out over mid-foot.
avoid: Leaning torso forward during the dip (causes bar to travel forward).
Dipping too deep or too slowly, losing the elastic stretch-shortening reflex.
Re-bending knees to catch the bar (push press requires catching with straight legs).

exercises.name: Pull-Ups
cues: Hang with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders in a full dead hang.
Initiate pull by depressing shoulder blades down and back ('pull shoulders into back pockets').
Drive elbows down toward floor, pulling upper chest toward bar until chin clears bar.
Lower under strict control back into a full dead hang before starting next rep.
avoid: Kipping, swinging legs, or using hip momentum to clear the bar.
Craning neck upward to touch bar while chest collapses.
Performing half reps by failing to lock out into a dead hang at bottom.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
cues: Retract shoulder blades into bench, plant feet firmly, and hold dumbbells over chest.
Lower dumbbells with control, maintaining vertical forearms and elbows tucked at 45–60°.
Lower into a deep, comfortable chest stretch at bottom without shoulder discomfort.
Press dumbbells up and slightly inward in a smooth arc, stopping just short of touching.
avoid: Clanking dumbbells together at top (removes muscular tension from pecs).
Flaring elbows perpendicular to torso ('T' position).
Allowing forearms to angle inward or outward.

exercises.name: Barbell Row
cues: Hinge at hips with torso angled at ~45 degrees, lower back flat, knees softly bent.
Take an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, bar hanging over mid-foot.
Drive elbows back behind torso, pulling bar toward lower abdomen / belly button.
Squeeze shoulder blades together at top, then lower bar under control into full stretch.
avoid: Jerking torso upright to heave weight (turning row into a standing shrug).
Rounding lumbar or thoracic spine under load.
Letting shoulders roll forward at the bottom of the rep.

exercises.name: Face Pull
cues: Set cable pulley to eye level with rope attachment; grip rope with thumbs pointing backward.
Step back into an athletic staggered stance with core braced and ribs pulled down.
Pull center of rope toward forehead while driving elbows high and wide.
Rotate hands back past ears into full external rotation, squeezing rear delts and upper back.
avoid: Craning head and neck forward to meet the rope.
Leaning backward or hyperextending lumbar spine to heave the weight.
Allowing elbows to drop below wrist level (internal rotation fault).

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
cues: Kneel on pad; tuck pelvis into posterior tilt, round upper back slightly, and brace abs hard.
Roll wheel forward under control, extending arms while keeping lower back from sagging.
Roll out only as far as core can maintain the hollow-body braced position.
Pull wheel back by contracting abs and engaging lats, keeping hips forward until reset.
avoid: Allowing lower back to sag into hyperextension (anterior pelvic tilt).
Sitting hips straight back onto heels to pull the wheel in (hip flexor cheat).
Rolling out further than abdominal strength can stabilize.

workouts.title: Conditioning & Core
workouts.focus: Front squat anterior strength, kettlebell swings, farmer carries, and jump rope

exercises.name: Barbell Front Squat
cues: Rest bar on front deltoids with fingertip clean grip (or cross-arm grip), elbows high and parallel to floor.
Maintain a vertical torso and brace core tightly throughout descent.
Squat between your knees to full comfortable depth, tracking knees forward over toes.
Drive floor away through mid-foot while keeping elbows driven high.
avoid: Elbows dropping downward, causing upper back to round and bar to dump forward.
Heels lifting off floor or weight shifting excessively onto toes.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
cues: Stand 1 foot behind bell; hike bell backward high between inner thighs like a football snap.
Drive hips forward explosively, snapping hips to standing with glutes and abs clenched.
Let kettlebell float to chest height purely from hip momentum; keep arms relaxed like ropes.
Let bell free-fall back into the hinge, waiting until forearms connect with inner thighs to hinge.
avoid: Squatting the knees forward instead of hinging hips back.
Actively lifting the bell with anterior deltoids and arms.
Leaning back and hyperextending lumbar spine at top of swing.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
cues: Deadlift weights to sides with a braced spine; stand tall with chest up and ribs down.
Pack shoulder blades down and back ('anti-shrug') with an intense crush grip.
Walk forward taking short, deliberate, controlled heel-to-toe strides.
Maintain rigid core tension, keeping weights motionless at sides without swinging.
avoid: Waddling or swaying torso side-to-side while walking.
Allowing shoulders to round forward or hyperextending lumbar spine.
Taking long, uncontrolled strides that cause weights to bang against legs.

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
cues: Hang from bar with an overhand grip, engaging shoulders down and back (active hang).
Squeeze legs together; curl pelvis upward toward chest as knees rise.
Pause for 1 second at top contraction with knees at chest level.
Lower knees under control to a dead stop before starting next rep.
avoid: Swinging legs or using hip momentum to kick knees up.
Arching lower back at the bottom of the rep.
Hanging passively with relaxed shoulders shrugged to ears.

exercises.name: Jump Rope
cues: Keep elbows pinned close to ribs, turning the rope primarily with relaxed wrists.
Jump lightly on balls of feet, clearing floor by only 1–2 inches per rotation.
Maintain soft knees and ankles to absorb impact with natural elastic rebound.
Keep breathing relaxed, rhythm steady, and torso tall.
avoid: Swinging whole arms from shoulder joints instead of turning with wrists.
Jumping excessively high or kicking feet backward (donkey kicks).
Landing stiff-legged or flat on heels.
